text:
Sam: FYI the nightly multi-node TP scaling job failed on 32 GPUs with a hard timeout, looks like a rank desync during an AllGather stage. CI: https://ci.internal.redwood/blue/organizations/jenkins/tp-scale/detail/1905123456

Lucy: saw the job, thanks. Which commit/sha? any kernel-selector changes in the last deploy?

Sam: sha: 8f3b2a4 (runtime/kernel-selector:enable-auto). No recent infra changes. Root log: 
```
2026-03-18 03:12:42,123 ERROR rank=17: ncclAllReduce timed out after 45s
2026-03-18 03:12:42,125 ERROR rank=3: rendezvous: expected 64KB, got 66KB
2026-03-18 03:12:42,130 FATAL rank=0: kvcache: kv_offset mismatch: local=524288 remote=524672
```

Jordan: attaching profiler summary from the failing run (nvprof + custom tracer). Allreduce wall time spikes at step ~2100 when seq lenses skew increases. numbers are ms per step: 
```
step 2096: allreduce=12.3 compute=35.2 overlap=8.1
step 2100: allreduce=143.9 compute=36.0 overlap=2.0   <-- spike
step 2104: allreduce=11.7 compute=34.8 overlap=9.0
```

Priya: That looks like comm/compute overlap lost because some ranks picked a different kernel path (maybe fallback to non-overlapped kernel). We saw the kernel-selector choose different kernels when sequence length quantization differs across micro-batches. Could be kvcache padding difference causing different seq lengths on different TP ranks.

Marta: +1 on kvcache padding hypothesis. We had a change last week that aggressively pads KV cache to 8-token boundaries for perf; if one node applies padding before batching and another after, offsets diverge.

Lucy: Can we repro locally with the same synthetic workload? Sam, can you share the exact config used (batching, pad, quantization flags)?

Sam: config snippet: 
```
MODEL=redwood-8b
TP=4
PP=1
BATCH_SIZE=2
KV_PAD=8  # new default
KERNEL_SELECTOR=auto
BATCHING_MODE=dynamic
```

Jordan: repro steps I used: run multi-node with the same seed, enable NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL, and runtime flag `--dump-kernel-decisions=/tmp/decisions.txt`. Command: 
```
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=DETAIL ./run_tp.sh --nodes 2 --gpus-per-node 16 --seed 42 --dump-kernel-decisions=/tmp/decisions.txt
```

infra-bot: CI job 1905123456 requeued (failed). Link: https://ci.internal.redwood/blue/organizations/jenkins/tp-scale/detail/1905123456/1/artifacts

Priya: If you can capture `/tmp/decisions.txt` and kvcache offsets at the same step (before the spike) we can diff the per-rank kernel choices and offsets. Look for lines like `rank=.. kernel=matmul_fused_v2 seq_len=512 kv_offset=524288`. If seq_len or kv_offset mismatch -> hang.

Sam: got a quick diff from the job artifacts: 
```
rank 0: kernel=matmul_v1 seq_len=512 kv_offset=524288
rank 17: kernel=matmul_v2 seq_len=520 kv_offset=524672
```

Marta: there it is. Kernel selector picked v1 vs v2 because seq_len differed due to KV_PAD applied at different stages. v2 isn't binary-compatible with v1 for the fused allreduce path which explains the desync and timeout.

Lucy: Proposed mitigations: 
- Short-term: force kernel selector to `model_compat` (fallback to common denom) or set `KV_PAD=0` in nightly until patch.
- Medium: make kernel selector canonicalize seq_len using post-batching normalized lengths before decision, or include kvcache offset/generation in rendezvous handshake to detect mismatch early and fail fast with a cleaner error.
- Long-term: ensure kvcache padding is deterministic across TP ranks (apply padding only after enter-batch boundary or centralize padding logic).

Jordan: I ran the repro with `KV_PAD=0` and forced `KERNEL_SELECTOR=compat`; run completed successfully twice. Allreduce timings stable: allreduce ~13ms.

Sam: I'll flip the nightly to `KV_PAD=0` and pin kernel selector to compat for the next 48h. Opening an incident tracker and a PR to fix kernel-selector canonicalization. Assigning to @Priya and @Marta for follow-up.

Priya: I'll own the kernel-selector fix, will add a unit test that simulates per-rank seq_len skew and asserts same kernel choice.

Marta: I'll add an ops check in the rendezvous to compare kv_offset headers and emit an early abort with a helpful msg (and link to runbook).

Sam: thanks everyone. Please paste any additional logs into the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
